original_question: For 0 <= beta < d, define the centered Hardy-Littlewood fractional maximal operator by M_beta f(x) = sup_{r>0} m(B(x,r))^{beta/d - 1} ∫_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, and define the uncentered fractional maximal operator analogously by taking the supremum over balls that contain x. When 0 <= beta < 1 and q = d/(d-beta), is the map f -> |∇M_beta f| bounded from W^{1,1}(R^d) to L^q(R^d)? The same question is asked for the uncentered fractional maximal operator.
target_in_paper: Section 5 (“Fractional maximal operators”), specifically Question 7, with nearby setup from Theorem 5.1 and follow-up context from Theorems 5.2 and 5.3. The chapter containing this material runs on pp. 69–92. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right operators, the ambient space \(\mathbb{R}^d\), the endpoint Sobolev source space \(W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)\), the target exponent \(q=d/(d-\beta)\), and the fact that the paper asks the same question for both centered and uncentered fractional maximal operators. In substance, it is very close to the paper’s Question 7. The main mismatch is that the paper asks this only for \(0<\beta<1\), not for \(\beta=0\). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
missing_details: The paper’s open problem is stated for the strict fractional range \(0<\beta<1\). The endpoint \(\beta=0\) belongs to the classical Hardy–Littlewood maximal-operator problem discussed earlier in Section 3, not to Question 7 in Section 5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))

The operators are defined on locally integrable functions \(f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^d)\), using open balls and Lebesgue measure; that ambient regularity assumption is implicit in your draft and should be made explicit in a stand-alone formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))

To make “bounded from \(W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)\) to \(L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)\)” fully stand-alone, the question should spell out that one seeks weak differentiability of \(M_\beta f\) together with an inequality of the form \(\|\nabla M_\beta f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)}\le C\|\nabla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}\) for all \(f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)\), with \(C\) depending only on \(d\) and \(\beta\). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))

The uncentered case should be stated as a separate parallel question for the uncentered fractional maximal operator, not merely as an informal afterthought, because Question 7 explicitly asks both versions side by side. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))

The nearby context matters: Theorem 5.1 explains that the remaining open endpoint regime is exactly \(0<\beta<1\), since the paper indicates that the case \(\beta\ge 1\) can already be handled by combining Sobolev embedding with the Kinnunen–Saksman regularity estimate. A paper-faithful stand-alone question should reflect that this is the residual endpoint case, not a general fractional-Sobolev problem for all \(\beta\). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))

If you want the question to be completely self-contained in the paper’s conventions, you may also note that the paper restricts to real-valued functions for simplicity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
refined_question:
Let \(d\ge 1\), let \(0< eta<1\), and set \(q=d/(d- eta)\). For a real-valued function \(f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^d)\), define the centered Hardy–Littlewood fractional maximal operator by \(M_ eta f(x)=\sup_{r>0}|B(x,r)|^{ eta/d-1}\int_{B(x,r)}|f(y)|\,dy\), and define the uncentered fractional maximal operator analogously by taking the supremum over all open balls containing \(x\). Is it true that for every \(f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)\), the functions \(M_ eta f\) and, respectively, the uncentered fractional maximal function are weakly differentiable and satisfy estimates of the form \(\|
abla M_ eta f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)}\le C\|
abla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}\) and \(\|
abla \widetilde M_ eta f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)}\le C\|
abla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}\), with \(C\) depending only on \(d\) and \( eta\)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
justification: The nearest official formulation in the paper is Question 7 in Section 5, which asks exactly for the endpoint derivative bound \(W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)\to L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)\) for the centered fractional maximal operator and separately for its uncentered analogue, with \(0<\beta<1\) and \(q=d/(d-\beta)\). The surrounding discussion in Theorem 5.1 explains why this precise range is isolated: the paper says the case \(\beta\ge 1\) is already covered by previously known regularity plus Sobolev embedding, so the unresolved endpoint is the interval \((0,1)\). Theorems 5.2 and 5.3 then record the nearest partial results: a complete one-dimensional answer for the uncentered operator and a higher-dimensional radial result for the uncentered operator. That is why the refined question should remain narrowly focused on this exact endpoint boundedness problem and should not be broadened beyond Question 7. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
